title: Canonical tensor mate and arbitrary constructible base change
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient setting [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\ge1$, and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes, without absolute separatedness; all arrows are $k$-morphisms. Use $D^b_{ctf}$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategory [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], on small pro-etale sites, and the derived pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For a separated finite-type arrow $u:T\to U$, write $F_u=Ru_!$, $G_u=Ru^!$ for compact supports and its transported constructible exceptional right adjoint [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], $\varepsilon_u:F_uG_u\to1$ for its counit, and $\omega_u=G_u\Lambda_U$. Use the specified canonical tensor map $\theta_{u,P}:Lu^*P\otimes^L\omega_u\to G_uP$ and dualizing base-change map $\beta_{u,v}$ of [def-pur-co-smoothness]; these maps are defined without assuming cohomological smoothness. All unit, symmetry and reassociation maps are the canonical derived ones.

Let $u:T\to U$ be separated of finite type, let $v:U'\to U$ be arbitrary between the finite-type $k$-schemes, and form the Cartesian square [def-cbc-compact-support-square] with $T'=T\times_UU'$, $w:T'\to T$, and $u':T'\to U'$. Use a compactification of $u$ and its base change. Write $E_u:v^*F_u\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{u'}w^*$ for the specified transported etale compact-support exchange [def-cbc-exchange-map]. For $P\in D^b_{ctf}(U,\Lambda)$, the pullback $Lv^*P$ is again bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude, with the same Tor interval. Define
$$b_{u,v;P}:Lw^*G_uP\longrightarrow G_{u'}Lv^*P$$
as the transported constructible adjoint transpose of
$$F_{u'}Lw^*G_uP\xrightarrow{E_u(G_uP)^{-1}}Lv^*F_uG_uP\xrightarrow{Lv^*\varepsilon_{u,P}}Lv^*P,$$
that is, the base-change morphism $b_{v,P}$ of [pur9-cs-def-bc] computed with the base-changed compactification for $u'$.
Then $b_{u,v;\Lambda_U}=\beta_{u,v}$ under the coefficient-unit comparisons, and the following equality of the specified canonical derived morphisms holds:
$$b_{u,v;P}\circ Lw^*\theta_{u,P}=\theta_{u',Lv^*P}\circ(1_{Lu'^*Lv^*P}\otimes\beta_{u,v}).$$
In this equation identify $Lw^*(Lu^*P\otimes^L\omega_u)$ with $Lu'^*Lv^*P\otimes^LLw^*\omega_u$ by the canonical tensor and pullback-composition comparisons. The exchange in the defining transpose is the same ambient proper-then-open exchange as in the compactification projection/exchange square, including for arbitrary $v$; it is not an independently chosen exchange. No cohomological smoothness of $u$ or $u'$, or invertibility of $P$, $\theta$, $b$ or $\beta$, is assumed.

proof.text: Use the already proved fixed-scalar pro-etale source-library APIs constructibleFiniteTor_leftDerivedFunctor_upperStar_obj and torAmplitudeIn_leftDerivedUpperStar. The former follows bounded constructible etale origins through the exact comparison/pullback square; the latter pulls back a flat model in the same interval. Their signatures allow any g and finite coefficients. Apply them to K and to each prescribed interval. This directly establishes the entire first conjunct in the stated fixed-coefficient presentation.

Install the compactification instances from c and its base change, and obtain quasi-compactness of f-prime from the pullback square. Unfold the unit-normalization predicate: the two arrows are definitionally equal by dualizingComplexBaseChangeMap, the component of rightDerivedUpperShriekBaseChangeMap at the coefficient unit followed by the canonical pullback-unit isomorphism. Thus rfl proves the second conjunct.

For arbitrary etale derived inputs M,N, apply the proved abstract Adjunction.projectionTensorMap_mateEquiv to the ordinary etale adjunctions. Supply projectionMap_rightDerivedLowerShriekBaseChangeMap as the actual projection/exchange square, the canonical tensor comparisons as delta-a and delta-b, and derivedSquareUpperStarIsoInvApp as kappa. Naturality in the first projection input is NatTrans.congr_app of projectionMap.naturality; tensor-pullback naturality is leftDerivedUpperStarTensorIso_hom_naturality_left. The exchange has its canonical inverse. This gives the private exceptional_tensor_base_change equality for any Cartesian square, without a smoothness assumption. These are existing proved source-library results, not new holed dependencies.

Specialize the first input M to the coefficient unit. The private unit_tensor_base_change lemma moves the left unitor through the base-change natural transformation, uses leftDerivedUpperStarTensorComparison_leftUnitor_hom, and applies naturality of the primed tensor mate to the canonical pullback-unit map. The interchange laws then give exactly dualizing_tensor_base_change in omega-first coordinates. Apply congrArg of comparisonUpperStar.mapDerivedCategory.map to this equality. Its two sides are definitionally the two sides of tensorMateBaseChangeIdentity, so it proves the last conjunct on every retained origin (in fact without the constructibility restriction). No theta, b or beta is inverted. The original coefficient-first interpretation and the unit route are unchanged.

Generic normalized exchange comparison identifies the actual proper factor, for arbitrary v. This is an operation or comparison tool, not a replacement for the cohomological-smoothness route.

Generic finite-coefficient projection isomorphism and its naturality are used, without assuming smoothness. This is an operation or comparison tool, not a replacement for the cohomological-smoothness route.
